thread.title: Republican candidate caught falsely claiming combat valor medal in startling 'pattern of deception' - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Republican candidate caught falsely claiming combat valor medal in startling 'pattern of deception' - NewsBreak

author: Samantha Loren
title: Republican candidate caught falsely claiming combat valor medal in startling 'pattern of deception' - NewsBreak
text:
By Samantha Loren ,
21 hours ago A Donald Trump-backed Nevada Republican is under fire over repeated campaign claims that he won a Bronze Star 'for valor.'
David Flippo's campaign blames staff errors, insisting the wording was a mistake rather than an attempt to mislead.
Flippo is running for Nevada's 2nd Congressional District, the heavily Republican seat being vacated by Representative Mark Amodei.
Trump endorsed him, hailing him as an 'America First Patriot' and giving him his 'Complete and Total Endorsement.'
That put Trump at odds with Amodei and much of the state party, who backed former state Senator James Settelmeyer.
Amodei has refused to endorse Flippo, dismissing him as 'not my cup of tea' and faulting his lack of Northern Nevada roots.
According to military records, Flippo received a Bronze Star for his service. The military also recognizes a separate valor distinction, the 'V' device, for acts of heroism during direct combat with an enemy.
That distinction is considerably rarer than a standard Bronze Star for meritorious service.
According to military records, Flippo received a Bronze Star for his service. The military also recognizes a separate valor distinction, the 'V' device, for acts of heroism during direct combat with an enemy A February 2026 fundraising email inaccurately claimed Flippo had 'earned the Bronze Star for valor,' language his campaign later acknowledged was incorrect. His spokesperson attributed the wording to a copywriter who 'accidentally' used outdated talking points Yet his campaigns have repeatedly described it as a Bronze Star 'for valor.'
The claim dates back to his 2023 run for Congress, when the narrator of his launch video called him a 'recipient of the Bronze Star that he received for valor.'
That video was only taken down after The Washington Post questioned the campaign about it.
The claim then resurfaced this year. In February, after Combat Vets for Congress endorsed him, a fundraising email said Flippo had 'earned the Bronze Star for valor.' Another appeal a week later used similar language.
His campaign now admits the descriptions were wrong, but it has offered two different explanations.
Spokesman Rory McShane told the Post that a copywriter had 'accidentally' recycled old talking points while churning out hundreds of fundraising solicitations.
Flippo blamed video editors instead. He said they had mistakenly merged his Bronze Star with another honor, the Outstanding Unit Award with Valor.
'Three years ago, our video editors made a mistake,' he said, adding that he regretted not checking the wording more closely.
Doug Sterner, a military-awards expert who has received two Bronze Stars, questioned the repeated use of the valor description.
'It's pretty sad that this is a multiple-time thing,' Sterner said. 'It shows a pattern of deception. It is someone trying to give an impression of their service that is not true.'
Jason Dempsey, a retired Army infantry officer and national-security fellow, also characterized the wording as a significant exaggeration.
Flippo served in the Air Force for 24 years, from 1985 to 2009, according to a 2025 interview. He worked as a maintenance and logistics officer and served as a logistics commander during the Iraq War.
His military service included overseeing the distribution of millions of gallons of aviation fuel used to support thousands of combat sorties and strategic airlift missions.
The Nevada Republican Party has defended Flippo amid the controversy. In a statement, the party said his campaign had confused his Bronze Star with the Outstanding Unit Award with Valor.
The party argued that the mistake does not diminish Flippo's military service or the decorations he earned, and criticized reporters for focusing on the wording error.
The Daily Mail has reached out to Flippo's campaign for comment.
